convoLines.text: "I asked Declan about the pantry run — Declan's gone. Still need hands. Are you in?"
"Another day like today and we're choosing who eats. Nobody's worked the american hazelnut patch past the treeline in days. We'll fill packs before dark."
There is no playable joint foraging outing yet. Giving food does not perform the promised outing.
"Sorry — I shouldn't load that on you. What's up?"
"This one — Yaupon Holly. Leaf, stem, smell. You won't forget it now."
"a burned farmhouse — I'll show you on the map sometime. It's real."
"Declan is gone and the world just... continues. That's the part I can't stand."
"Someone should watch your back. Might as well be me."
You show them Jerusalem Artichoke — where it grows, how to tell it apart. A short laugh. "And I've been walking past it for weeks."
"Come see what I found. You won't believe it."
Ruby shows you where they go to think. "Don't tell the others. Everyone needs one place."
"I sit apart to eat. It doesn't bring anyone back. It just keeps my hands from shaking."
"Oh — okay. Later, then."
"...Sorry, lost my train of thought."
"This was good." They mean it.
"What scares you most about what's happening? The real answer."
They go quiet. "Yeah. Me too. The randomness would almost be kinder."
"That we're interesting to it. Being watched means being kept. I'd rather be boring to the sky. Boring things get left alone."
"Still on what scares you most."
"Okay. Yeah. I trust you."
"Forget I said anything. What did you want?"
"Huh. Let me think about that." "Since Declan died... I keep expecting to see Declan at the fire. Stupid."
"Sleep's gone strange. I braid grass while listening to plans at odd hours now. Whatever gets me to morning."
"Well." A breath. "That's where things stand."
"They're already drifting away. "Later."
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
"About the pantry run — still need hands. Are you in?"
"...Sorry, lost my train of thought."
"Hm. Never mind — go on."
"a spring that runs clear — I'll show you on the map sometime. It's real."
"You want to know about that? Okay." "Last time things were different. They always are." "I dreamed Declan was still here. Woke up angry at the dream. Stupid."
They hear the warmth in it. They're not ready to let it in.
"I sit apart to eat for Declan, now. Feels right. Feels like the least I can do."
"Anyway." A small smile.
"Still on what's been happening."
You show them Fly Agaric — where it grows, how to tell it apart. "Huh." They turn it over in their mind. "I'll remember that one."
"Sure. I'll be around."
"...Actually, forget it."
"...Where was I? Gone. Ask me something else."
"We never finished talking about what's been happening — we left it mid-thought, 4 days back. 'A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.'"
"Nobody says Declan's name right yet. We will. Give it a few days."
They nod slowly, not quite done, not quite continuing.
"Still on what's been happening."
Something in them almost softens — then doesn't. Not yet.
You show them Jerusalem Artichoke — where it grows, how to tell it apart. They nod slowly, committing it to memory. "Good to know. Really good to know."
"Right. Go on, then."
"...Sorry, lost my train of thought."
"We never finished talking about what's been happening — we got cut off, 7 days back. 'You show them Jerusalem Artichoke — where it grows, how to tell it apart. They nod slowly, committing it to…'"
"Walk with me? I want another pair of eyes on something."
You walk to the tree line with Shannon. Nothing much there — but they talk the whole way, and you learn the shape of them a little better.
"My part? I braid grass while listening to plans and stay ready."
"So." They look at the fire for a moment.
"As I said — Still on what's been happening."
"...Sorry, lost my train of thought."
"Yeah? What's up?"
"Huh. Let me think about that." "I'd follow you out past the treeline. Don't tell the others — they'd want to come too."
"Sure. I'll be around."
"Hm. Never mind — go on."
«¡Hola! ¿Cómo te llamas?»
"Saw things with too many joints. Give them room. That's the whole lesson."
«De acuerdo.» — Luis translates: "Agreed." They nod back, slowly.
«Gracias. De verdad, gracias.» — Luis translates: "Thanks. Truly, thanks." A grin breaks through, quick and warm.
«Eres buena persona.» — Luis translates: "You're a good person." You tap your chest, then theirs. Us. They nod, emphatic. "Water?"

«¿Dónde se duerme aquí?» — Luis translates: "Where does one sleep here?"
They glance toward their own thoughts; the exchange is winding down.

"This was good." They mean it.

"I did the count twice. The count doesn't change. Nobody's worked the old burn east of camp in days. We'll fill packs before dark."
